1) The radiation from the LWFA stage is mainly due to the electron beam, not the plasma, 2) The radiation spectrum of the LWFA stage peaks at the plasma frequency, 3) The radiation spectrum from the 1.5 and 12 GeVs stages peaks at the plasma and laser frequencies, respectively, and 4) The radiation spectrum is dominated by the self‐injection process
the radiation from a LWFA stage is mainly produced by a few electrons that are injected in the wakefield, and that the radiation from the LWFA stage can be described in terms of two distinct regimes.

the radiation from 1.5GeV and 12 Gev laser‐plasma accelerators is dominated by a narrow beam of synchrotron radiation, which is emitted from the electron beam, and a broad beam of bremsstrahlung radiation, which is produced from the interaction between the electron beam and the plasma.

the radiation from the 12 GeV stage is more energetic and has a more directional spectrum than the one from the 1.5 stage, while the radiation from the latter is more intense, has a wider spectrum, and is emitted from the whole acceleration stage.
the radiation in 1. GeV LWFA stage is dominated by a single narrow band spike, which can be explained by the radiation of the electron beam.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the radiation from LWFA stages is very similar to that of conventional accelerators.
, for the 1.5‐GeV stage, the radiation from the self‐injection electrons is the dominant source, while for the 12‐GeV stage, both self‐injection and beam‐driven electrons contribute to the radiation.

the radiation from the 1.5‐GeV stage is mainly produced by electrons that are injected into the wake and accelerated, while in the 12‐GeV stage the radiation comes from the electrons that are accelerated in the wake without injection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation from a LWFA stage has a very distinctive spectral signature, which is different from that of a conventional accelerator.
radiation from LWFA stages can be used to study the self‐injection physics and to infer the properties of the electron bunch, such as the bunch charge, the bunch length and the bunch energy spread.
the radiation signature from a single LWFA stage is very different from that of a single laser‐plasma interaction.
